notes:
Overview: QuantumShelf is a mid-market SaaS vendor providing a conversational support layer for e-commerce merchants. They plan to replace a brittle keyword-based search and heuristic reranker with dense retrieval + learned reranking.

Key ask (verbatim): 'We need sub-200ms retrieval + top-5 quality parity with our human-curated picks — agents can't wait.'

Scale: planning to index ~6M canonical tickets (normalized), + ~20M FAQ/snippet rows from merchant KBs -> ~26M vectors expected. Current infra: PostgreSQL + hybrid vector store (pilot with Pinecone).

Performance targets: p50 end-to-end retrieval+rerank < 60ms, p95 < 200ms for standard queries; burst QPS target 400 qps for agent console flows; backlog nightly reindex window 02:00-05:00 PST. Cost target: <= $0.02/query (end-to-end) for typical multi-step workflow.

Model preferences & architecture notes: prefer open/quantized reranker (distil-encoder or small cross-encoder distilled to pointwise/rerank top-100), retrieval using 1536-d embeddings (open model) with HNSW + shard-aware routing; fallbacks to a cheaper semantic-only retrieval when heavy load. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching + quantization profiles.

Security/compliance: SSO via SAML (Okta), SOC2 in procurement checklist, need audit logs shipped to their Splunk instance, KMS integration for at-rest keys, contractually required EU data residency for specific EU merchants.

POC scope: 1) Ingest 3M sample tickets + 1.2M KB rows; 2) Run retrieval+rerank perf at 200 qps sustained; 3) Evaluate top-5 rerank MRR/precision vs. baseline; 4) Validate VPC peering + security controls.

Customer sentiment: enthusiastic but pragmatic — engineering lead emphasized 'we'll buy if you can show predictable tail latency and a clear cost model.'

Past decisions: evaluated Pinecone (failed to meet rerank co-location needs), piloted an in-house FAISS cluster (scales but ops-heavy). They want Redwood to remove ops burden and give repeatable SLOs.

Links referenced in calls: pricing deck (drive link), security questionnaire, and two Fireflies transcripts for product deep-dives.
